dm: Just as the thought of "I" has arisen Toward this selfless body through habituation, Why should the thought of "I" not likewise Arise toward other sentient beings through habituation?
gm: Just as towards this selfless body The mind of "I" has arisen through habituation, Likewise, towards other sentient beings as well, Why would the mind of "I" not arise through habituation?

dm: Therefore, when acting for the benefit of others, No sense of conceit or wonderment will arise, Just as when one has eaten food oneself, No expectation of a reward arises.
gm: If it is like that, the benefit of others, Even when done, amazement and conceit do not arise, Just as when one has eaten food oneself, There arises no hope for a reward.

dm: Therefore, just as I protect myself From even the slightest unpleasantness, I should likewise cultivate a protective mind And a mind of compassion toward the world.
gm: Therefore, just as to a small degree I protect myself even from unpleasant words, Likewise, a mind of protecting transmigratory beings and A mind of compassion should be habituated.

dm: Therefore, the Protector Avalokiteśvara, Out of great compassion, In order to dispel the fears of beings in cyclic existence, Blessed even his own name.
gm: Therefore, the protector Avalokiteśvara, Out of great compassion, for transmigratory beings, In order to dispel the fears of the assembly, Blessed even his own name.

dm: One should not turn back from hardships; For through the power of such habituation, Even that whose very name once caused fear, Becomes something one is unhappy to be without.
gm: One should not turn back from difficulties, For by the power of habituation in this way, Even someone whose name one feared to hear, Without them, one becomes joyless.

dm: Whoever wishes to quickly provide protection For both themselves and others, Should practice the supreme secret: The exchanging of oneself and others.
gm: Whoever, regarding oneself and others, Wishes to quickly protect them, The exchange of self and others, Which is the supreme secret, should be practiced.

dm: Because of attachment to this body of mine, Fear arises even toward small things that cause alarm; Who would not detest as an enemy This body that gives rise to such fear?
gm: Through attachment to this body of mine, Fear arises at even small sources of fear; Towards that body which gives rise to fear, Who would not be hostile as if towards an enemy?

dm: Desiring to perform the rituals to heal The body’s ailments, such as hunger and thirst, People kill birds, fish, and deer, Or lie in wait along the paths.
gm: For whichever body's illnesses like hunger and thirst, Wishing to perform the treatment to cure them, Birds, fish, and wild animals Are killed and ambushed on the road.

dm: If those who, for the sake of profit and honor, Kill even their own fathers and mothers, And steal the property of the Three Jewels, Will be burned in the Incessant Hell,
gm: Whoever, for the sake of profit and respect, Kills even their father and mother, and, Having stolen the wealth of the Three Jewels, Will therefore burn in the Incessant Hell;

dm: What wise person would desire, Protect, and make offerings to such a body? Who would not view it as an enemy, And treat it with contempt?
gm: What wise person, towards that body, Would desire, protect, and venerate it? Towards this, who, as if towards an enemy, Would not look and not despise it?

dm: Thinking, "If I give this away, what will I have to enjoy?" Is the way of a demon, thinking only of one's own benefit. Thinking, "If I use this myself, what will I have to give?" Is the Dharma of the gods, thinking of the welfare of others.
gm: "If I give, what will I consume?"— Thinking of one's own purpose is the way of a demon. "If I consume, what will I give?"— Thinking of others' purpose is the quality of a deity.

dm: If one harms others for the sake of oneself, One will be tormented in the hells and other lower realms. If one harms oneself for the sake of others, One will attain all forms of excellence.
gm: If, for one's own sake, one harms others, One will be tormented in hell and so forth. If, for others' sake, one harms oneself, One will obtain all excellences.

dm: One who desires high status for oneself Will be reborn in the lower realms, in wretchedness, and as a fool. If that very desire is transferred to others, One will attain good migrations and be honored.
gm: Through wishing for oneself to be exalted, One will fall to bad migrations and become base and foolish. If that very thing is shifted to others, One will obtain happy migrations and respect.

dm: If one employs others for one's own benefit, One will experience servitude and the like. If one employs oneself for the benefit of others, One will experience lordship and the like.
gm: If one employs others for one's own purpose, One will experience servitude and so forth. If one uses oneself for the purpose of others, One will experience lordship and so forth.

dm: Whatever happiness there is in the world, It all arises from desiring the happiness of others. Whatever suffering there is in the world, It all arises from desiring one's own happiness.
gm: Whatever happiness there is in the world, All of that arises from wishing for others' happiness. Whatever suffering there is in the world, All of that arises from wishing for one's own happiness.

dm: What need is there to say more? Observe the difference between these two: The childish who work for their own sake, And the Sages who work for the sake of others.
gm: What need is there to say much? Childish beings act for their own purpose, and The Sage acts for the purpose of others. Look at the difference between these two!

dm: If one does not truly exchange One's own happiness for the suffering of others, Buddhahood will not be attained, And there will be no happiness even in cyclic existence.
gm: One's own happiness and the sufferings of others, If one does not perfectly exchange them, One will not achieve Buddhahood, and Even in cyclic existence there will be no happiness.

dm: Setting aside the next life, Even the goals of this life will not be achieved, Just as a servant will not do his work And a master will not pay his wages.
gm: Let alone the next world, With servants not doing their work and Masters not paying wages, Even the purpose of this life will not be accomplished.

dm: Having abandoned the perfect happiness That achieves well-being in both the seen and the unseen, Through the cause of inflicting suffering on others, The deluded take up unbearable misery.
gm: Of that which accomplishes seen and unseen happiness, Entirely abandoning the excellent joy, Through the cause of inflicting suffering on others, The foolish take on unbearable suffering.

dm: Whatever harm exists in the world, And however many fears and sufferings there may be, If they all arise from grasping at a self, Then what use is that great demon to me?
gm: Whatever harm there is in the world, and However much fear and suffering there is, If all of that arises from grasping at a self, What use is that great demon to me?

dm: If I do not completely let go of the self, I will be unable to abandon suffering, Just as one who does not let go of fire Is unable to avoid being burned.
gm: If one does not completely let go of oneself, One cannot abandon suffering, Just as if one does not let go of fire, One cannot avoid being burned.

dm: Therefore, in order to pacify harm to myself And to pacify the suffering of others, I shall give myself away to others And cherish others as I do myself.
gm: Therefore, to pacify harm to myself and To pacify the suffering of others, I should give myself to others and Hold others as myself.

dm: O mind, you must understand with certainty: "I am now under the power of others." Except for the welfare of all sentient beings, You must now think of nothing else.
gm: "I am under the control of others"— O mind, you should definitely know this, and Apart from the purpose of all sentient beings, Now you should not think of anything else.

dm: It is not right to achieve your own ends With eyes and so forth that belong to others; It is not right to act for your own sake With those eyes and so forth that are for their sake.
gm: With eyes and so forth that are under the control of others, It is not appropriate to accomplish one's own purpose. With eyes and so forth that are for their purpose, It is not appropriate to act wrongly toward them.

dm: Therefore, make sentient beings your primary concern; Whatever you see upon my body, Snatch it away and use it To act for the benefit of others.
gm: Therefore, sentient beings should be made principal, and Whatever I see on my body, Having taken it away, I will use it to benefit others.

dm: Having identified oneself with those who are inferior and so forth, And having identified others as oneself, With a mind free of conceptual doubt, Meditate on envy, rivalry, and pride.
gm: Having made the lower and so forth into oneself, and Having made oneself into the other, With a mind free of conceptualization, I should meditate on jealousy, rivalry, and pride.

dm: "This one is honored, but I am not; I have not obtained such things as this. This one is praised, while I am reviled; This one is happy, while I am suffering."
gm: This one is respected, but I am not. I have not found wealth like this one, and This one is praised, while I am disparaged. This one is happy, but I am suffering.

dm: "I am the one who does the work, While this one remains in a state of ease. This one is renowned as great in the world, While I am known as lowly and without merit."
gm: I do all the work, and This one abides in happiness itself. This one is great in the world, and I am known as inferior and without good qualities.

dm: What is the use of one who lacks good qualities? I myself am fully endowed with good qualities. There are those compared to whom this person is inferior, And there are those compared to whom I am superior.
gm: What can be done about being without good qualities? All of us are indeed endowed with good qualities. There are those compared to whom this one is inferior, and There are those compared to whom I am supreme.

dm: The decline of my ethical discipline, views, and so forth, Is due to the power of the afflictions and is not under my control. I must be healed as much as possible, And I shall even accept the hardship involved.
gm: The decline of discipline, view, and so forth Is due to the power of afflictions; it is not under my control. I should be healed as much as possible, and I will willingly accept even harm.

dm: If, however, I am not the one to be healed by him, Why does he treat me with contempt? What use are his good qualities to me? I am the one who possesses good qualities.
gm: However, if I am not to be healed by this one, Why does he despise me? What use are his good qualities to me? This one himself possesses good qualities.

dm: Lacking compassion for beings who dwell in the jaws of the miserable realms, He is outwardly conceited about his qualities, And wishes to challenge the wise.
gm: Abiding in the jaws of the vicious lower realms, This one is without compassion for beings. Outwardly conceited about his good qualities, He wishes to contend with the wise.

dm: Looking at one who is equal to himself, In order to make himself superior, He will certainly secure his own gain and honor, Even through contention.
gm: Having looked at those equal to me, In order to make myself superior, My wealth and respect Will definitely be established even through dispute.

dm: I shall ensure that my own good qualities Are made known to the entire world, While ensuring that no one ever hears Of any good qualities he may possess.
gm: By all means, my good qualities Will be clear to the whole world, and Furthermore, whatever good qualities this one has, I will ensure that no one hears of them.

dm: I shall conceal my own faults, And I shall be the one who is honored, not he. I shall secure great gain today, And I shall be the one who is respected, not he.
gm: My faults will also be hidden, and I will be venerated, but not this one. Today I have well found wealth, and I will be respected, but not this one.

dm: I shall watch with long-lasting delight As this person is brought to ruin. I shall make him the laughingstock of all beings, And the object of their mutual derision.
gm: Upon this one being made miserable, I will look with joy for a long time. He will be the laughingstock of all beings, and Mutual disparagement will be brought about.

dm: It is said that this miserable one is even competing with me. But is he my equal in learning, wisdom, Physical appearance, lineage, or wealth?
gm: This miserable one is even renowned To be contending together with me. Are his learning and wisdom, or Form, caste, and wealth equal to mine?

dm: Having heard of my own virtues Being proclaimed to all in this way, I shall experience the thrill of joy that makes my hair stand on end, And I shall fully enjoy that happiness.
gm: Thus proclaimed to all, Having heard of my good qualities, Thrilled with the arising of joy, I will fully enjoy happiness and well-being.
